canonical_reference: Wang et al. 2024, NAACL Findings 2024 (arXiv:2309.04766)
languages: Chinese; English; Filipino; Indonesian; Malay; Singlish; Spanish; Vietnamese
evidence_note: Suite of 29 datasets (13,263 samples): majority are pre-existing natively sourced per-language sets (classic NLP = 8,382 samples), so Native and Universal by majority composition; minority components Cross-MMLU/Cross-LogiQA are translated from English and four cultural subsets are natively built.

canonical_reference: Zhang et al. 2023, NeurIPS Datasets & Benchmarks 2023 (arXiv:2306.05179)
languages: Afrikaans; Chinese; English; Italian; Javanese; Portuguese; Thai; Vietnamese
evidence_note: 12,317 questions harvested from official national exams in 9 languages (~23% require images); exam content retains each country's social-cultural context. Paper reports 9 languages; 8 names verified in sources opened, the 9th was not enumerated there.

canonical_reference: Vayani et al. 2025 (arXiv:2411.16508)
evidence_note: 22.7K image QA pairs in 100 languages / 73 countries; content rendered into the languages via GPT-4o translation with 800+ hours of native-speaker verification and correction; 13 of 19 domains are cultural (food, festivals, heritage, religion), i.e. culture-specific content across many countries, not one region. 100 language names not enumerated in sources opened.

canonical_reference: Lovenia et al. 2024, EMNLP 2024 (arXiv:2406.10118)
evidence_note: Dual-nature resource: a data hub cataloguing ~500 existing Southeast Asian corpora plus a benchmark suite over 36 indigenous SEA languages and 13 tasks; coded Benchmark for the evaluative suite. Aggregates existing natively sourced corpora. Count = 36 benchmark languages per abstract (body text reports 38/39; hub spans ~1,000 languages).

canonical_reference: Conneau et al. 2018, EMNLP 2018 (arXiv:1809.05053)
languages: Arabic; Bulgarian; Chinese; English; French; German; Greek; Hindi; Russian; Spanish; Swahili; Thai; Turkish; Urdu; Vietnamese
evidence_note: MultiNLI development/test sets professionally human-translated into 14 further languages (7,500 pairs per language); designed set spans tiers, so no single tier coded.

canonical_reference: Aggarwal, Gupta & Kunchukuttan 2022 (arXiv:2204.08776)
languages: Assamese; Bengali; Gujarati; Hindi; Kannada; Malayalam; Marathi; Odia; Punjabi; Tamil; Telugu
evidence_note: English XNLI data machine-translated (IndicTrans) into eleven Indic languages, with translation quality checked by human evaluation; content remains the English XNLI/MultiNLI genres.

canonical_reference: Amirkhani et al. 2023, Soft Computing (arXiv:2009.08820, 2020)
evidence_note: 10,367 Persian NLI samples generated from 3,539 Persian multiple-choice exam questions plus natural web sentences; paper explicitly frames it as a native alternative to translation-based NLI datasets.

canonical_reference: Ebrahimi et al. 2022 (arXiv:2104.08726; EMNLP 2021)
languages: Asháninka; Aymara; Bribri; Guaraní; Nahuatl; Otomí; Quechua; Rarámuri; Shipibo-Konibo; Wixarika
evidence_note: XNLI examples human-translated from the Spanish XNLI set into 10 Indigenous languages of the Americas by translators/community members; the paper's title explicitly characterizes them as truly low-resource languages; content is translated MultiNLI genres.

canonical_reference: Urbizu et al. 2022, LREC 2022
evidence_note: GLUE-style suite of 10 tasks assembled from pre-existing Basque datasets (Basque news, Twitter, Wikipedia), so majority native; the FMTOD intent/slot subsets derive from translated data (minority). Basque is characterized as a low-resource language in the sources consulted.

canonical_reference: Kakwani et al. 2020, Findings of EMNLP 2020 (IndicNLPSuite)
languages: Assamese; Bengali; Gujarati; Hindi; Kannada; Malayalam; Marathi; Odia; Punjabi; Tamil; Telugu
evidence_note: NLU benchmark spanning several tasks (news category classification, headline prediction, Wikipedia section-title prediction, multiple-choice QA, NER, cross-lingual sentence retrieval) for 11 Indic languages, assembled from natively sourced Indic-language news and Wikipedia data.

canonical_reference: Doddapaneni et al. 2023, ACL 2023
evidence_note: Nine NLU tasks, 105 evaluation sets (ACL version: 20 languages); the paper states human annotators were used to curate OR translate the datasets and no majority split is published, so Mixed. Language names not enumerated in sources opened.

canonical_reference: Timilsina et al. 2022, LREC 2022 (NepBERTa)
evidence_note: First Nepali NLU evaluation benchmark (NER, POS tagging, content classification, categorical pair similarity) built from Nepali corpora alongside NepBERTa; Nepali is explicitly framed as low-resource in the sources consulted. Introduced in 2022 — the roster year 2025 conflicts with the primary source.

canonical_reference: Cross-lingual Cross-temporal Summarization: Dataset, Models, Evaluation (arXiv:2306.12916; Computational Linguistics)
evidence_note: Corpus of historical fiction texts with Wikipedia summaries in English and German (hEn-De 289 and hDe-En 328 instances, plus monolingual variants); document-summary pairs are natively occurring, not translations of a source set. Small evaluation corpus with reported model benchmarks (dual dataset/benchmark nature).

canonical_reference: Perez-Beltrachini & Lapata 2021, EMNLP 2021
evidence_note: Wikipedia (document, lead-section summary) pairs natively written in each language and aligned by entity across 4 languages in 12 directions; the authors set up a benchmark with baselines on the corpus.

canonical_reference: Zhang & Eickhoff 2024, LREC-COLING 2024 (arXiv:2303.04092)
evidence_note: Over 24,000 English technology-news articles with 18,000 human-written Chinese summaries collected as naturally occurring cross-lingual pairs; the paper's stated contrast is with CLS datasets built by translation. Title calls it a benchmark dataset (dual nature).

canonical_reference: Ladhak et al. 2020, Findings of EMNLP 2020 (arXiv:2010.03093)
languages: Arabic; Chinese; Czech; Dutch; English; French; German; Hindi; Indonesian; Italian; Japanese; Korean; Portuguese; Russian; Spanish; Thai; Turkish; Vietnamese
evidence_note: Article-summary pairs extracted from human-authored WikiHow guides in 18 languages, aligned cross-lingually via the images illustrating each step — not translations.

canonical_reference: Shi et al. 2022 (arXiv:2210.03057)
languages: Bengali; Chinese; English; French; German; Japanese; Russian; Spanish; Swahili; Telugu; Thai
evidence_note: First 250 GSM8K grade-school math problems human-translated from English into 10 typologically diverse languages; the designed set spans high- and low-resource languages, so no single tier coded.

canonical_reference: Son et al. 2025 (arXiv:2502.17407)
evidence_note: Multilingual Competition Level Math: a translated collection of competition problems (MATH500 and AIME 2024, originally Olympiad problems) in 55 languages. Language names not enumerated in sources opened.

canonical_reference: MaXIFE: Multilingual and Cross-lingual Instruction Following Evaluation, ACL 2025 (DOI 10.18653/v1/2025.acl-long.698)
evidence_note: 1,667 verifiable instruction tasks as parallel prompts across 23 languages, built from English instruction sets following a documented translation strategy; instruction following matches none of the named task classes, so Other. 23 language names not enumerated in sources opened.

canonical_reference: Liu et al. 2025 (arXiv:2505.10089; Findings of EMNLP 2025)
evidence_note: Cross-lingual RAG benchmark built from recent news articles in English plus Arabic, Chinese, German and Spanish; the paper's baseline design (replacing the translated question with its original English) shows the non-English question sets are translations of English originals, while the grounding articles are native per language.

canonical_reference: Raihan et al. 2025, NAACL 2025 (arXiv:2410.15037)
evidence_note: The 164 HumanEval prompts rendered into 204 natural languages (the FLORES-200 set) by machine translation with quality assurance; expert human translations exist for 15 languages only, so the majority composition is translated. 204 language names not enumerated in sources opened.

canonical_reference: CL-HumanEval: A Benchmark for Evaluating Cross-Lingual Transfer through Code Generation, PACLIC 2024
evidence_note: HumanEval docstrings translated into Japanese with GPT-4o mini (the English version was also switched to LLM-generated text for fairness); evaluates cross-lingual transfer into Python code generation.

canonical_reference: Doddapaneni et al. 2024, Cross-Lingual Auto Evaluation for Assessing Multilingual LLMs (arXiv:2410.13394)
languages: Bengali; French; German; Hindi; Telugu; Urdu
evidence_note: RECON is the CIA (Cross Lingual Auto Evaluation) Suite's human-annotated test set: 500 instructions with human judgment scores across six languages, with questions/responses in the target languages (translated from English) and reference answers/rubrics in English. Roster year was blank; filled from the source (arXiv, Oct 2024).

canonical_reference: Singh et al. 2024, ACL 2024 (arXiv:2404.16816)
evidence_note: Multi-way parallel generation suite (CrossSum-In, Flores-In, XQuAD-In, XorQA-In) extending existing English benchmarks to 29 Indic languages through human translation/annotation; multi-task suite, so Other; content derives from the source benchmarks. 29 language names not enumerated in sources opened.

canonical_reference: Kim et al. 2025, COLM 2025 (arXiv:2503.01996)
evidence_note: Seven synthetic RULER-style retrieval/aggregation tasks; English instructions were written first and then translated with native speakers into 25 further languages, with haystack content generated per language from the translated templates. 26 language names not enumerated in sources opened.

canonical_reference: Enevoldsen et al. 2025, ICLR 2025 (arXiv:2502.13595)
evidence_note: Community-driven aggregation of 500+ existing per-language text-embedding evaluation tasks across 250+ languages; the refined benchmark selection explicitly removes machine-translated datasets, so the majority composition is natively sourced existing data. The paper states 250+ languages, so no exact count is coded.

canonical_reference: Adelani et al. 2024 (arXiv:2406.03368; NAACL 2025)
evidence_note: Human-translated subsets of XNLI, MGSM and MMLU for 17 typologically diverse African languages the paper explicitly calls low-resource; three distinct task families (NLI, math reasoning, multiple-choice knowledge QA), so Other. Per-task language counts vary (15-17) and names were not enumerated in sources opened; the v1 abstract said 16 languages, the v2/NAACL version says 17.

canonical_reference: Asai et al. 2023 (arXiv:2305.14857; NAACL 2024)
evidence_note: Unifies 15 existing tasks across 54 languages in a sequence-to-sequence format; the underlying task data are datasets annotated in each language (natively sourced) and only the instructions were additionally machine-translated. 54 language names not enumerated in sources opened.
